new_statements.quote: As already noted in §2.2.2, tone is distinctive in Grassfields languages and, as such, has been marked in the data. For the sake of space, this has been done on the vocalic segments using the diacritics [...] to represent high, mid, low, and related contour (rising and falling) tones. Because a proper tone analysis has not been done on any of these languages other than Aghem, the marking system should not be looked on as anything more than an impression of pitch.
new_statements.citation: Thormoset, David. 2007. Phonological reconstruction and the Aghem central vowels. MA thesis, University of Calgary. xii+153 pp. (also posted by SIL Cameroon; our bibliography dates it 2000/2006)
new_statements.locator: p. 60 (§3.1, data presentation; pdf p. 68 of the silcam copy we hold); supporting: p. 41 (§2.2.2), p. 35 (§2.2 scope)
new_statements.check: not checked by the second reader
new_statements.relation_note: Treats all five A810 languages, Bu included, as tone languages and tone-marks the Bu data (H, M, L, contours) while warning that no tone analysis exists for Bu; p.41: 'Grassfields languages, like the majority of Bantu, are tonal' and floating tones cannot be reconstructed for the non-Aghem languages for lack of frame data; also gives Bu phonotactics (p.62: Bu allows only three coda consonants; p.75: 'Bu does not permit /n/ in coda'; Bu infinitive prefix e-). 'Stress' occurs only in diachronic speculation about Pre-Bantu/Aghem stem-initial stress (pp. 23, 63, 134), not as a synchronic claim about Bu.
new_statements.rule_in_words: Bu (Laimbue), like the other West Ring A810 languages, is treated as a tone language with lexically distinctive tone; the thesis marks surface pitch (H/M/L/contours) on its Bu wordlist but makes no phonemic tone analysis and no statement about word stress or accent.
new_statements.exceptions: Author cautions that mid-tone marks are impressionistic ('not an assertion that these languages have a fundamental mid tone -- they likely do not') and that floating tones could not be established outside Aghem.
new_statements.identity_note: Not a new discovery -- already held and read (READALL 2026-09-18, tag 'read: silent on stress'); re-listed here because A's search was for stress OR tone and this is the only opened work with first-hand Bu data and a tone remark whose scope includes Bu. p.35 §2.2: 'The primary focus of this study is the data from Aghem, Bu, Isu, Weh and Zhoa' (SIL Africa Area 1700-item wordlists recorded Jan 2004 by Nelson Tschonghongei & D. Thormoset for the Aghem Language Development Committee); p.4/ALCAM 810 'Aghem, Bu (Laimbu), Cha', Isu..'. Bu here = the Laimbwe village south of Wum (A810/West Ring), not Lower Fungom Buu. Glottolog has the work (West Ring table, tagged under Aghem, listed by Glottolog as an overview/comparative), not under laim1240.
